IV. Key Findings
1. Invoice Number Reuse: 173 payments flagged (66.3%)
Suggested follow-up: Obtain both invoices sharing the reused number. Confirm whether the vendors are the same entity operating under
different names, or distinct entities. If distinct, investigate how the same invoice number was accepted by the AP system for two different
vendors.
2. Weekend Payments: 70 payments flagged (26.8%)
Suggested follow-up: Review the entity's IT general controls for automated payment processing that may coincide with weekends.
Distinguish between automated ACH runs (lower risk) and manual weekend disbursements (higher risk requiring authorization review).
3. Payment Before Invoice: 35 payments flagged (13.4%)
Suggested follow-up: Obtain management explanation for each prepayment. Confirm whether a prepayment arrangement was
authorized per AP policy and supported by a contract or purchase order. The absence of authorization documentation may indicate a
control gap that the engagement team should consider as part of their professional assessment of the AP control environment.

The automated revenue recognition testing procedures documented in this workpaper were performed on the revenue
transaction detail provided by management for the period under examination. These procedures are designed to identify
potential data anomalies that may warrant further investigation by the engagement team. The analysis was performed with
reference to the FASB Accounting Standards Codification and applicable professional auditing standards.

II. Methodology
The following automated tests were applied to the revenue GL extract with reference to professional auditing standards
(ISA 240: Auditor's Responsibilities Relating to Fraud — presumed fraud risk in revenue recognition, ISA 500: Audit
Evidence, PCAOB AS 2401: Consideration of Fraud). Where contract data columns were detected, additional
contract-aware tests were applied per ASC 606 / IFRS 15 revenue recognition standards. Results represent revenue
anomaly indicators, not fraud detection conclusions:
 Test
Tier
Description
Large Manual Revenue
Entries
Structural
Flags manual revenue entries of $50,000 or more (a fixed Paciolus default
threshold, not performance materiality). Revenue is a presumed fraud risk under
ISA 240.
Year-End Revenue
Concentration
Structural
Flags revenue concentrated in the last days of the period, a common revenue
recognition anomaly indicator.
— 3 —
Prepared using Paciolus Diagnostic Intelligence. Does not constitute an audit, review, or attestation engagement.
Test
Tier
Description
Round Revenue Amounts
Structural
Flags revenue entries with round dollar amounts that may indicate estimated or
manually entered values rather than actual contracted amounts.
Revenue Sign Anomalies
Structural
Flags debit balances in revenue accounts (normally credit), indicating potential
mispostings or contra-revenue entries requiring investigation.
Unclassified Revenue
Entries
Structural
Flags revenue entries missing account classification (unmapped to chart of
accounts).
Z-Score Outliers
Statistical
Uses z-score analysis to identify revenue transaction amounts that are statistically
unusual relative to the other revenue entries in the population tested.
Revenue Trend Variance
Statistical
Compares the period’s net revenue total with the prior-period total supplied by the
auditor and flags a change above the configured percentage (Paciolus default
30%). Skipped when no prior-period total is provided.
Revenue Concentration
Risk
Statistical
Flags single accounts representing a disproportionate share of total revenue.
Cut-Off Risk
Statistical
Flags revenue entries recorded within a configurable window of the period-end
date, where timing of recognition is most susceptible to error or manipulation (ISA
240 cut-off fraud risk indicator).
Prior-Period Timing
Statistical
Flags revenue entries recorded within a configurable window (Paciolus default 3
days) of the period-start date, where revenue belonging to the prior period may
have been booked late. Distinct from the period-end cut-off test; skipped when the
period boundaries cannot be determined.
Benford's Law Analysis
Advanced
Applies Benford’s Law first-digit analysis to revenue transaction amounts.
Duplicate Revenue Entries
Advanced
Flags revenue entries with identical amount, date, and account — potential
duplicate postings.
Contra-Revenue Anomalies
Advanced
Flags elevated returns/allowances relative to gross revenue, a fraud risk indicator.
Contract Data
Completeness (ASC 606
Step 1)
Advanced
Contract data completeness check informed by ASC 606 Step 1. Flags an entry
that carries a contract ID without a performance obligation ID, a recognition
method without a contract ID, or point-in-time recognition without an obligation
satisfaction date. It checks only that these fields are populated; it does not evaluate
whether a contract exists or is valid. Skipped when no contract-aware columns are
detected.
Recognition Before
Satisfaction
Contract
Flags entries where available contract data suggests a performance obligation
under ASC 606 may not have been satisfied prior to the recognition date.
Missing Obligation Linkage
Contract
Flags revenue entries that carry a contract ID but no performance obligation ID, or
a performance obligation ID but no contract ID, in the source data.
Modification Treatment
Mismatch
Contract
Flags contracts whose entries record more than one modification treatment, or
only some of which record a modification. ASC 606 / IFRS 15 can require
different treatments for different modifications, so a flag may warrant review
rather than indicating non-compliance.
Allocation Inconsistency

II. Methodology
The following automated tests were applied to the fixed asset register with reference to professional auditing standards
(ASC 360-10: Property, Plant, and Equipment, ISA 500: Audit Evidence, ISA 540: Auditing Accounting Estimates —
depreciation methods, useful life, and residual value estimation, PCAOB AS 2501: Auditing Accounting Estimates).
Results represent fixed asset anomaly indicators, not depreciation adequacy conclusions:

Fully Depreciated Assets
Structural
Flags assets where accumulated depreciation equals or exceeds cost (NBV zero or
negative), indicating potential ghost assets or items requiring disposal review.
Missing Required Fields

date), a data completeness anomaly indicator.
Negative Values

Over-Depreciation
Structural

Useful Life Outliers
Statistical

bounds, configurable). Useful life is an accounting estimate (ISA 540); the bounds
themselves are a Paciolus convention, not set by ISA 540.

Uses z-score analysis to identify fixed assets with acquisition costs that are

configured z-score threshold from the mean cost are flagged for review as
potential overstatement or data entry anomalies.
Asset Age Concentration
Statistical
Flags disproportionate concentration of total asset cost in a single acquisition year,
indicating potential bulk capitalization anomalies.
Depreciation Recalculation
Statistical
Sprint 682: Recalculates expected depreciation from cost, residual value, useful
life, and depreciation method. Flags variance >5% (straight-line) or >15%
(double-declining balance) from expected accumulated depreciation per IAS 16 /
ASC 360.
Duplicate Assets
Advanced
Flags assets with identical cost, description, and acquisition date — potential
duplicate capitalization or double-counting.

Flags assets whose recorded residual (salvage) value exceeds 30% of original cost
(a Paciolus default, configurable), or is negative. Residual value is an accounting
estimate (ISA 540); the 30% bound is a Paciolus convention, not set by ISA 540.
Lease Asset Indicators
Advanced
Scans asset descriptions for keywords suggesting operating or finance leases
(lease, ROU, right-of-use, leasehold). Flagged items should be confirmed for
proper ASC 842 / IFRS 16 right-of-use asset treatment.
